title: Access Concierge + Policy Scoring Pipeline for Enterprise Admin Requests
creator: Lina Zhang
description:
Background: Enterprise customers repeatedly submit unstructured admin and access requests (RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML integrations, SCIM provisioning fixes, org policy exemptions). This causes long cycle times (multi-day handoffs) and escalations to SEs and engineering. Problem: intake is noisy, lacking prioritization and contextual artifacts; follow-up requires manual investigations across logs, tenant config, and audit trails.

Goal: Build an "Access Concierge" intake pipeline that: (1) auto-classifies request type and business impact via a policy-scoring model, (2) pre-collects relevant artifacts (tenant metadata, recent audit events, support logs, last successful SCIM sync), (3) suggests owner/team (Security/Identity/Platform/SE) and SLA, and (4) surfaces a curated workbench for operators with recommended actions and rollback steps. This pipeline must integrate with Support/CRM, internal Linear/GitHub flows, and the Console request UI.

Non-goals: full RBAC UI redesign, over-automation of destructive changes, or replacing security approvals for privileged grants.

Constraints: must respect customer privacy (PII minimization), align with compliance for enterprise customers, and be configurable per-tenant policy thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: New intake form in Console or Support captures required structured fields for admin requests (request type, affected org/team, justification, urgency, requester role).
Automated classifier assigns one of: Low / Medium / High impact and recommends owner team with >= 75% historical accuracy on sampled dataset.
System attaches minimum artifact bundle to ticket: tenant config snapshot (non-PII), last 48h audit events, latest SCIM sync status, and account owner contact.
Routing integration: tickets for High impact go to Enterprise Ops triage queue with 4-hour SLA; Medium to Platform SME with 24h SLA; Low to self-serve guidance.
Operator workbench shows recommended mitigation steps, required approvals, links to runbooks, and one-click actions for creating change requests.
All intake events logged to the Console audit log with retention policy and scoped KMS encryption as per enterprise requirements.
tasks: Design structured intake schema for RBAC / SSO / SCIM / policy-exemption requests (PM + Design).
Prototype policy-scoring heuristic and training dataset using historical support tickets (PM + Research).
Implement pre-collection service that snapshots tenant metadata and audit events (ENG-23111).
Build routing rules and Linear integration to create triage issues with artifact links (ENG).
Create operator workbench UI and link runbooks (Design + Eng).
Add telemetry and cost/latency tracking for artifact collection; privacy review and KMS integration.
Pilot with 3 existing enterprise customers and collect SLA & quality feedback.
updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after a sequence of escalations from two enterprise customers requesting role mass-provisioning and an emergent SCIM outage. Initial requirements captured with Customer Success. (Lina Z).
2026-03-03: Kickoff with Design and Eng. Decision to scope initial MVP to classification + artifact pre-collection; deferring in-line automated role changes to a later iteration. (Carlos M).

2026-03-05: Research pulled 420 historical admin/access tickets; built preliminary labeling heuristics. Early classifier prototype achieves 0.72 F1 on validation. Need more labeled examples for SSO edge cases. (Research).
2026-03-08: Security and Compliance reviewed data collection plan; requested PII minimization and per-tenant opt-out flag. Added to acceptance criteria. (Priya N, Security).
2026-03-10: ENG-23111 dependency identified: pre-collection microservice must support sampling rate controls and tenant-scoped credentials. Engineering estimates 3 sprints. (Carlos M).
2026-03-12: Design mockups for Console intake form ready; focusing on minimizing friction for CS & customers. Pilot plan drafted for two customers C1 and C2 for April. (Design).
decisions: MVP will not perform automated destructive RBAC changes; it will provide curated, auditable recommended steps for operators.
Classification model will be a hybrid: heuristic rules for immediate routing + ML model for nuanced cases (privacy-safe features only).
Artifacts attached to tickets will exclude raw PII; where needed, pointers to encrypted blobs accessible to authorized operators will be used.
risks: Classifier false negatives on High-impact requests could cause SLA breaches and customer outages.
Over-collection of sensitive data could violate customer compliance; must enforce strict minimization and access controls.
Operator workload could increase if recommended actions are insufficiently prescriptive; require runbook quality assurance.
outcome_metrics: Mean time to first triage action (target: < 4 hours for High impact).
Percentage of tickets with complete artifact bundle on creation (target: >= 90%).
Operator time-to-resolution reduction for admin requests (target: 30% faster).
Customer satisfaction on escalations in pilot (target NPS delta +6).
